facts.text: Hannastown grew around the first county seat of Westmoreland County, founded in 1773 and home to the first English courts west of the Allegheny Mountains.
Robert Hanna, a pioneer trader, built a tavern beside Forbes Road in 1769, giving the town its name and serving as a frontier hub.
In 1775, the Hanna's Town Resolves were adopted here, echoing the spirit of Lexington and Concord and signaling early American patriotism.
A 1782 raid by Seneca and British forces burned Hanna's Town, a dramatic event that underscored the town’s role in frontier conflicts.
Today, the Westmoreland History Education Center—opened in 2019—houses the town’s museum, library, and research gallery, preserving its Revolutionary‑era legacy.
The historic site spans 180 acres and features a reconstructed tavern, three relocated log houses, a fort, and an authentic 18th‑century Conestoga wagon.
